parsed.main_gap: The core of the lower bound (Lemma 4) — the tree-component/signed-sum claim — is asserted with 'standard; details omitted', leaving the crux of Liu's guarantee unproved.

errors.description: Lemma 4's essential step is not proved. One must observe that the number of pairs (edges) is at most n < n+1 vertices, hence some component is a tree/isolated vertex, then use its bipartition to sign the pieces. None of this counting or construction appears; the existence of V_T and signs with |Ξ| ≤ Σε_i + [M odd]a_M is simply asserted.
errors.quote: By a tree-component argument on the multigraph whose vertices are the original pieces $0,1,\dots,n$ and whose edges are the pairs $P_i$, there is a set $V_T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$ and signs $s:V_T\to\{\pm1\}$ such that the signed sum $\Xi:=\sum_{j\in V_T}s(j)\,q_j$ satisfies $|\Xi|\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted).

errors.description: Supporting evidence for the omitted lemma is numerical (Monte Carlo / grid search), which carries no proof weight; the write-up leans on it in place of the missing argument.

parsed.notes: Answer and reduction are correct; Lemma 2 (picking phase) and Lemma 5 (upper bound construction, including the mark count ≤ n and the pairing argument) are carefully and correctly proved. Only the lower-bound core is missing.
